correctness.rationale: The exact state and edge definitions lead to the complete 5-band adjacency table. The included integer Bellman potential proves all distances on the infinite periodic cover, not merely on a finite sampled graph; quotient-lift minimization then reduces finite distances to two integer formulas. Four-step induction with fully checked boundary inequalities yields the eccentricity formulas for every integer m>=4. Two separately written Python scripts replay independent direct forcing enumerations m=4..10 and the complete symbolic tail and induction certificate. Residual risk is confined to proof-replay and correctly maintaining the stated graph conventions.

value.rationale: Minimum zero-forcing sets are natural smallest propagation-capable sensor placements, and changing one sensor is an intrinsically motivated move. Complete sharp change distances, all-state eccentricities, and a mod-four radius/diameter law for a classical structured infinite graph family are more informative than the earlier known zero-forcing number and configuration symmetry types. The periodic-cover technique supplies a reusable way to study local reconfiguration metrics. No downstream theorem or publication-scale contribution is assumed.
